content: Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and therapeutic effect of dolutegravir by inducing hepatic metabolism through UGT1A and CYP3A enzymes. This interaction can be mitigated by co-administration with lopinavir/ritonavir, darunavir/ritonavir, or atazanavir/ritonavir. Avoid using dolutegravir with etravirine unless one of these protease inhibitors is co-administered. Etravirine significantly decreases the levels and efficacy of dronedarone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of duvelisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers decreases duvelisib's area under the curve (AUC), potentially reducing its therapeutic effect. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine increases the plasma concentration and effect of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Dose adjustment may be required. For deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment, reduce the edoxaban dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). Efavirenz increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A inducers should be avoided as it may reduce the efficacy of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of eliglustat by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers significantly reduce eliglustat exposure, and co-administration is not recommended. Etravirine interacts with elivaldogene autotemcel, potentially reducing the effects of both drugs. Patients should discontinue antiretroviral therapy (ART) at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization medications and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Etravirine increases the plasma concentration and effect of elvitegravir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease elvitegravir plasma concentrations and lead to therapeutic failure or resistance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of encorafenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of entrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of enzalutamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of erdafitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It may also increase erdafitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ergotamine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin base increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases erythromycin base levels. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases erythromycin ethylsuccinate levels. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases erythromycin lactobionate levels. This combination is contraindicated. Erythromycin stearate increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine decreases erythromycin stearate levels. This combination is contraindicated. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of everolimus by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of fedratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The effect of co-administering a strong CYP3A4 inducer with fedratinib has not been studied. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of fentanyl by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to reduced fentanyl efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in physically dependent patients. After discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine increases the plasma concentration and effect of fexinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4, which may increase the risk of adverse effects of CYP3A4 substrates. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of finerenone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fluvoxamine increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of fostamatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of fruquintinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, continue fruquintinib at the recommended dosage. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of ganaxolone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose but do not exceed the maximum daily dose for weight. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of glasdegib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of ibrutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers decrease ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately 10-fold. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of idelalisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as they significantly reduce idelalisib systemic exposure. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Concomitant use is contraindicated unless indinavir is boosted with low-dose ritonavir. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of infigratinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of irinotecan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of irinotecan liposomal by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Isoniazid increases the plasma concentration and effect of etravirine by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of istradefylline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ivabradine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of ivacaftor by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as systemic exposure to ivacaftor is substantially reduced (~9-fold). Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of ivosidenib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates or replace with alternative therapies. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of ixazomib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong inducers decrease ixazomib Cmax by 54% and AUC by 74%. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inducers. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of larotrectinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inducers is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose. Resume the prior dose once the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued for 3-5 half-lives. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of lefamulin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers unless the benefit outweighs the risks. Monitor for reduced efficacy. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of lemborexant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of lenacapavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of leniolisib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lorlatinib reduces the plasma concentration and efficacy of etravirine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine decreases the plasma concentration and efficacy of lovastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Etravirine interacts with lovotibeglogene autotemcel, potentially interfering with its manufacturing. Discontinue antiretroviral therapy (ART) at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting ARTs may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination.
